en.title: Concrete and abstract nouns
en.summary: A concrete noun names something you can see or touch; an abstract noun names an idea, quality or feeling.

paragraphs: A concrete noun names something you can see, hear, touch, smell or taste. An abstract noun names an idea, a quality, a state or a feeling. You cannot touch freedom or fear, but you can talk about them. Abstract nouns are common in writing about ideas.

Many abstract nouns are made from adjectives or verbs with a suffix such as -ness, -ity, -ment, -tion, -ship or -th. Many abstract nouns are uncountable, so they take no plural and no a or an. We say Honesty is important, not An honesty is important.
Some nouns can be abstract or concrete. Beauty is abstract, but a beauty is a beautiful person or thing. Experience as an idea is uncountable, but an experience is one event.

An abstract noun often takes the verb be and an adjective: Fear is natural. It can also follow a preposition: She is full of joy. In writing, prefer a clear concrete example next to a difficult abstract idea.

items: Wrong: **An honesty is important.** Right: **Honesty is important.**
Wrong: **I need an information.** Right: **I need some information.**
Wrong: **She has many kindnesses.** (as a quality) Right: **She has great kindness.**

ro.title: Substantive concrete și abstracte
ro.summary: Substantivul concret denumește un lucru palpabil, iar cel abstract denumește o idee sau un sentiment.

paragraphs: Substantivul concret denumește o ființă sau un lucru pe care îl putem percepe prin simțuri. Substantivul abstract denumește o idee, o calitate sau un sentiment. Ambele tipuri au gen și număr în limba română.

Multe substantive abstracte se formează din adjective, din verbe sau din alte substantive. Adăugăm sufixe specifice precum -ătate sau -ețe la cuvântul de bază. La fel ca substantivele concrete, ele primesc articol hotărât sau nehotărât.
